extracted.intended_audience: people suffering from 'nerves' (nervousness/nervous breakdowns) and general readers seeking self-help health guidance
extracted.subtask_description: Practical, layperson-directed regimen of diet, outdoor exercise, sleep, play, and emotional regulation intended to cure and prevent 'nervous' disorders (neurasthenia) and maintain long-term mental and physical health.

rubrics_metrics.name: Daily outdoor exercise (duration)
rubrics_metrics.description: The nervous individual ... should get out of doors at least three or four hours a day, every day in the week.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a general rule; even those who work for a living should arrange to spend that much time outdoors in wholesome recreation. After recovery, continue such outdoor exercise to prevent relapse. Anti-pattern: thinking short streetcar rides or indoor shopping count as outdoor exercise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remove the cause — diet correction
rubrics_metrics.description: You have first to remove the cause, and that is largely wrong diet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendation of a lacto-vegetarian diet (milk, fruits, vegetables); avoid meat and eggs (author hasn't eaten them for ten years). Examples: Bulgarian peasants thrive on milk/fruits/vegetables. Anti-patterns: relying on single 'miracle' foods (buttermilk tablets) instead of changing overall diet.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regular, ample sleep
rubrics_metrics.description: Go to bed at an early hour and get eight or nine hours of sleep not only some nights but every night in the week.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if initially sleepless, retire early; the relaxed body rests even without sleep. Nervous people may benefit from nine or even ten or eleven hours. Children: up to ten or twelve hours, but should get up when they wish. Sleep environment: sleep on a sleeping porch or keep windows wide open day and night.

rubrics_metrics.name: Daily play and laughter
rubrics_metrics.description: The nervous individual ... should play some game. Play compels one to laugh and laughter is needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Find mild games (tossing a ball, playing with children) to encourage laughing and jovial conversation. Anti-pattern: giving up play in adulthood; excessive seriousness correlates with wrinkles and unhappiness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer mild, non-violent exercise
rubrics_metrics.description: Any form of outdoor exercise or play is good for the nervous person if it is not violent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid violent sports that make the heart 'beat like a trip-hammer' (tennis is too violent; regular basket ball game is too violent for the nervous person). Emphasize mild outdoor activity that raises spirits without overtaxing the heart.

rubrics_metrics.name: Walking as primary exercise
rubrics_metrics.description: Walking slowly in the open air for two or three hours is the best exercise for man.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Walking is free and available to all; when possible, have a definite place to go and an agreeable companion for stimulating conversation. Systematic daily walking is superior to intermittent long walks (e.g., only on Sundays).

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific recommended activities (practical examples)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use practical, mentally-engaging outdoor activities: basket-ball tossing, sawing wood, small workshop carpentry, gardening, care of chickens, bicycling (with caution), golf (if time and access).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sawing wood builds muscles and engages many muscles without harm; many sanitariums charge for such work but it can be done at home. A small workshop provides concentration beneficial for nerves. Gardening and tending chickens provide purposeful outdoor exercise. Bicycling is good but main roads may be dangerous.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid high-altitude and strenuous mountain climbing
rubrics_metrics.description: Mountain climbing ... is not to be recommended for most people suffering from 'nerves.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High altitudes often make nervous people more restless; in mountains, be out of doors but take things easy—prefer level walks or slow pace. Leisure and patience are emphasized in hill country; do not overexert or strive to reach summits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pace and leisure as therapy
rubrics_metrics.description: Let leisure be your watchword in a hill country ... take things easy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cultivate patience, avoid impatience and hurry. Use leisure to reduce nervous strain; adopt a leisurely attitude like a burro when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain regimen during vacations and after recovery
rubrics_metrics.description: Nervous people should, if possible, take a vacation once a year and get into new surroundings ... stick to his rules just as rigidly as when he is at home.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Changing surroundings help but do not replace diet and exercise rules. After recovery, continue the changed habits to prevent relapse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sleep environment and year-round exposure
rubrics_metrics.description: If possible, sleep the year round on a sleeping porch. If you don't possess a porch, then, have all the windows in your sleeping room wide open day and night.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fresh air during sleep is presented as beneficial. This complements the advice for ample, regular sleep.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regularity and daily habit (consistency over sporadic effort)
rubrics_metrics.description: You must have exercise every day and must have some play along with it. You can't keep fit if you exercise only one, two, or three days a week.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anti-pattern: thinking a long country walk on Sunday suffices. Emphasize daily, systematic practice of regimen.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correct chewing and temperance in eating
rubrics_metrics.description: Dieting, temperance in eating, and the careful chewing of food ... when beginning to diet and take outdoor exercise he should go to bed regularly ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chew food to a cream; the manner and amount of eating count as much as the kind of food. Temperance in appetite and diet supports nerve recovery and general health.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid miracle cures, patent medicines, and fads
rubrics_metrics.description: Buttermilk tablets ... are of no benefit whatever. The buttermilk-tablet route will not take you there.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not substitute sensational or miraculous cures for principled diet and outdoor living. Institutional treatment may help initially, but long-term cure requires habit change. Anti-pattern: credulous acceptance of 'sucker' remedies by physicians and laymen.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat dental, tonsillar, and eye problems promptly
rubrics_metrics.description: If you have any bad teeth you should at once go to a good dentist ... if your tonsils have become mere pus sacs you will have to ... have them removed ... if you need glasses, you cannot hope to get well ... until your eyes are properly fitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address specific physical defects (teeth, tonsils, eyesight) with appropriate specialists (dentist, nose & throat specialist, oculist, aurist) because these impede recovery. These measures apply to all people, nervous or not.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use mild therapeutic adjuncts for constipation if needed
rubrics_metrics.description: If for a time you have to take physic, it is best to take some hot mineral water half an hour before breakfast ... eating enough apples, usually overcomes constipation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjuncts like hot mineral water or increased fruit (apples) can help bowel regularity while maintaining diet/exercise regimen.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social and conversational support with a humorous slant
rubrics_metrics.description: If a number of people afflicted with 'nerves' could get together and take daily walks and at the same time determine that their conversation should always have a humorous slant, it would help all of them wonderfully.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Companionship and humor during walks or play are mentally stimulating and therapeutic. Seek agreeable companions who sustain uplifting, rapid-fire talk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid indoor-only 'outings' and sedentary substitutes
rubrics_metrics.description: Many of our women today ... go on a diet and stick to it, but they will not get out of doors. ... they ride a little distance in a street car or in an automobile to do some shopping. ... Some of them seem to think that is taking outdoor exercise, but of course it is not.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Actual time spent outdoors in active recreation is required; passive or transport-based outings do not substitute for outdoor exercise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mindful selection of activities by gender/occupation needs
rubrics_metrics.description: Sewing, and especially fine needlework, is very trying to a woman's nerves, and if she has broken down under that kind of work she should quit it and do something else. If she has to make her living in that way, she ... should observe the outdoor rules as well as rules for dieting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommend alternative activities when vocation or domestic duties are nerve-straining. Both men and women can adopt workshops, gardening, or mild games adapted to their circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moderate use of automobiles for outdoor exposure
rubrics_metrics.description: Riding in an automobile is beneficial if the machine is driven slowly and the patient is kept out of doors from three to four hours. But the fast driving that is generally done is bad for these people.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Automobile trips should be slow and extended to achieve outdoor exposure; high-speed rides are harmful to nervous persons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of purposeful manual work to build strength
rubrics_metrics.description: For the nervous man who is able to do it, I know of nothing better to build up muscles and keep the liver and other internal organs in good shape than sawing wood. ... Wood sawing brings into play every muscle in the body.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical, purposeful manual tasks that engage the body and mind (wood sawing, workshop projects) are therapeutic and inexpensive compared with institutional 'work therapy.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Emotional regulation — control anger, envy, suspicion
rubrics_metrics.description: Fight anger as you would poison ... Anger will hurt you ... get control of your temper. ... Never suspect folks. It is useless.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop self-control and patience as central aims: they temper emotions that 'poison' the nerves. Cultivate living for others (children) rather than self; shifting focus helps recovery and long-term happiness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attitude and purpose — live for others and regain childhood joy
rubrics_metrics.description: Have the courage to believe that you are going to get well. ... If you are a mother ... live for them. ... Get your mind off yourself and your troubles and on the children of this world, and keep it there. ... Go back to the memories of your childhood. Be with children and play with them all you possibly can.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopting an outward-focused purpose (caring for children, helping others) and reconnecting with childlike play and memories are recommended therapeutic attitudes that support recovery from 'nerves'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combine diet and exercise — neither alone suffices
rubrics_metrics.description: Outdoor exercise alone will not cure such people ... You must bestir yourself. You must get out of doors, and above all, you must eat right.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both corrected diet and consistent outdoor exercise (plus sleep and emotional management) are required. Institutional treatments may initiate improvement but lasting cure requires changing lifelong habits.
